messages:
Noah Miller: Quick heads-up 11 VoltCommerce wants a 7-10 day POC to prove a compat proxy for their incumbent vendor. Top asks: token-for-token billing parity, stop-token semantics, and a short secQ. Can SEs + security scope?

Priya Patel: I can run the POC. Need their canonical prompt list (40), a set of 12 failure cases, and their billing examples. Also confirm latency target - they asked for median <150ms, p95 <300ms in staging.

Sam Ortiz: We should clarify "token-for-token" meaning: do they expect exact token counts reported by our system, or exact invoice line items? If it's exact counts, we must run their tokenizer or replicate its quirks in the shim.

Tess Nguyen: Adapter surcharge alert 1 If we run their tokenizer in the shim it'll add CPU and latency. Recommend: fixed POC fee + usage + small adapter surcharge (we usually quote 6-8% CPU uplift). I'll draft options.

Noah Miller: They specifically called out stop diversity (they use prioritized multi-stop rules) and expect us to honor the first-match semantics. Also asked for X-TraceId passthrough so their observability continues to work.

Priya Patel: Example shim curl we can hand them (maps vendor args -> Redwood API):

```bash
curl -X POST https://shim.volt.stage/api/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <VOLT_POC_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"List recent charges for account 88","stop":["\n\n","END"],"max_tokens":80,"temperature":0.0}'
```

Priya Patel: Shim responsibilities: map max_tokens->max_new_tokens, run vendor tokenizer to compute reported token_count, echo X-TraceId, and implement prioritized stop semantics. We'll emit a token_report in response headers for their billing reconciliation.

Jordan Kim: Ops notes: if they want logs exported to their bucket for reconciliation, we can enable S3 delivery with a 7-day retention. Will need their allowlist CIDR and IAM role for cross-account writes. That will be in the ops runbook.

Olivia Sanchez: SecQ notes: they attached a 9-page questionnaire. Key asks: KMS integration, key custody, SOC2 Type II, pen-test, data residency, and no plaintext storage of customer secrets. I'll take the lead on answers. Drop any technical artifacts you want included.

Sam Ortiz: For strict token parity we have two approaches: (A) run their tokenizer inside the shim and echo the vendor token_count (accurate, CPU cost), or (B) normalize inputs to our tokenizer heuristics (cheaper, approximate). If their finance insists on exact parity we'll do (A).

Tess Nguyen: Commercially, option A implies a small engineering surcharge and we recommend using a short-lived sandbox with fixed commit so we can predict costs. I'll prepare numbers: fixed engineering fee + projected usage.

Noah Miller: Timeline they requested: sandbox in 48h, 4 days of canonical runs, 2 days of tuning, 1 day sign-off. Is that feasible?

Priya Patel: Yes. Proposed milestones:
- Day 0-2: provision sandbox + allowlist + upload prompts
- Day 3-6: run canonical suite and collect diffs
- Day 7-8: parity tuning (stop tokens, tokenizer edge cases)
- Day 9: acceptance meeting + deliverables (diff CSV, latency report, secQ answers)

Priya Patel: Deliverables example: CSV with columns: prompt_id, vendor_text, redwood_text, token_delta, sim_score, notes. We'll run an embedding-similarity score and flag sim_score < 0.82 for manual review.

Jordan Kim: Also include latency histogram and p95/p99 for token lengths. Ops will attach allowlist steps, IAM role sample, and S3 bucket policy for cross-account delivery.

Olivia Sanchez: For KMS: we support external key wraps and customer-managed keys for Private deployments. For hosted POC we can enable envelope encryption with our KMS and not persist raw keys. I'll note that in secQ and mention SOC2 + pen-test dates.

Sam Ortiz: One more technical ask: should we enable deterministic mode (seed + temp=0) to reduce variance during billing parity checks? If they accept deterministic outputs, it's easier to match vendor outputs.

Noah Miller: I'll ask the customer about accepting deterministic mode for the verification runs only.

Tess Nguyen: Action items: Priya to push shim harness + minimal repo link, Tess to send pricing options, Olivia to start secQ draft, Jordan to prepare ops runbook for allowlist & S3. Target: sandbox ready in 48h.

redwood-deploy-bot: Sandbox 'voltcommerce-poc-07' provisioned (sbx-211). Credentials uploaded to vault; access granted to thread participants.

Priya Patel: Starting harness now. Will post repo link and a sample token_report header format: X-Token-Report: total=123;vendor=123;redwood=123;delta=0

Noah Miller: Great. We'll sync with VoltCommerce tomorrow @ 11am PT. :rocket:
